hooks.text: Astronauts aboard the space station watch 16 sunrises every day.
Sixteen sunrises greet astronauts in orbit every single day.
Astronauts in space do not get just one sunrise daily.

title: Why Astronauts See 16 Sunrises Every Day
description: Orbiting Earth at 17,500 miles per hour, astronauts aboard the International Space Station experience 16 sunrises and sunsets every single day.

beats.text: Astronauts aboard the space station watch 16 sunrises every day.
beats.visual: Astronaut looking through windows of Cupola observation module at Earth limb, 2021
queries: Astronaut in Cupola International Space Station

beats.text: Picture living inside a Boeing 747 jumbo jetliner.
beats.visual: Boeing 747 jumbo jet airliner flying high in the sky, 2018

beats.text: Now stretch its exterior across a full American football field.
beats.visual: Full exterior view of the International Space Station against Earth, 2010
queries: International Space Station full view STS-132
ISS full exterior from Space Shuttle

beats.text: Place that massive station 250 miles above Earth's surface.
beats.visual: International Space Station orbiting high above Earth atmosphere, 2015
queries: International Space Station high altitude orbit

beats.text: Now fling it across orbit at 17,500 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Time lapse of Earth surface passing rapidly below the station, 2019

beats.text: At that speed, it circles the entire planet every 90 minutes.
beats.visual: Orbital sunrise over Earth horizon viewed from the station, 2020
queries: Orbital sunrise from International Space Station

beats.text: This means they cross from day to night every forty-five minutes.
beats.visual: Orbital terminator line showing day and night over Earth, 2021

beats.text: That is why astronauts in orbit watch 16 sunsets every day.
beats.visual: Orbital sunset silhouette view of solar arrays against Earth horizon, 2022

better_than_last: Refined the mid-script orbital transition beat to explicitly detail the forty-five-minute day-night crossing as requested by the reviewer, improving clarity and logical flow.
